rootCauseAnalysis.summary: The traffic-gen replica is unavailable because its readiness probe and application loop repeatedly fail against web-frontend:8080/healthz. The namespace deny-all ingress NetworkPolicy selects all pods and is consistent with blocking the required traffic path, while the backend service and application are healthy.
causalChain: Why? The sole Pod `traffic-gen-6fbdd9f844-c7cqm` is Running but readiness is False, and its readiness probe targets `web-frontend.demo-frontend:8080/healthz`.
Why? The traffic generator's own logs show `probe=success` initially, then repeated `probe=failure`, while the web Deployment remains 2/2 Ready with ready Service endpoints.

Why? Namespace NetworkPolicy `default-network-policy` selects every pod and enables ingress policy without any ingress allow rules, blocking ingress to selected pods; this is consistent with the probe failure.

Root cause: `demo-frontend/default-network-policy` has an ingress-isolation configuration with no allowed ingress sources, preventing the traffic-gen readiness path from succeeding. Direct packet-level confirmation was unavailable because pod exec and Prometheus access were blocked.

dueDiligence.targetAccuracy: The target is the NetworkPolicy whose ingress configuration must be changed to allow the required traffic, rather than the Deployment that only reports the symptom. A workflow can add a narrowly scoped ingress allowance.
dueDiligence.proportionality: The issue is isolated to the readiness path and has a specific policy configuration fix. The NetworkPolicy is more precise than changing replica counts, probe timing, or the healthy web Deployment. Any required ingress exception should be narrowly scoped to the relevant traffic.
dueDiligence.scopeCompleteness: Inspected the incident Deployment, owning ReplicaSet and Pod, its events/logs/current and previous-log path, downstream Service, EndpointSlice, web Deployment and two representative web Pod logs, ConfigMap, NetworkPolicy, node usage, and owner/remediation context. Prometheus was attempted but inaccessible; packet-level tests were blocked.
dueDiligence.causalCompleteness: Traced Deployment -> ReplicaSet -> Pod -> readiness probe -> downstream Service/Endpoints -> NetworkPolicy. The deepest verified configuration cause is the empty ingress allow-list in `default-network-policy`; exact CNI enforcement and packet direction could not be verified.
dueDiligence.evidenceSufficiency: Deployment, ReplicaSet, Pod, Service, EndpointSlice, downstream Deployment, ConfigMap, events, node metrics, and NetworkPolicy were inspected. Evidence supports readiness failure and healthy backend. Assumptions: the observed NetworkPolicy is enforced by the active network plugin and is the specific blocker. Pod exec was forbidden (`create pods/exec`); Prometheus discovery/series timed out; node stats-summary was forbidden (`get nodes/proxy`).
dueDiligence.regressionAwareness: No prior remediation history is available for `demo-frontend/NetworkPolicy/default-network-policy`; the target context showed no tier-1 or tier-2 remediations and no regression detected.
dueDiligence.alternativeHypotheses: Considered unhealthy web backend and missing Service endpoints; contradicted by `web-frontend` 2/2 Ready, two ready EndpointSlice entries, HTTP-200 `/healthz` ConfigMap, and clean startup logs. Considered scheduling, image pull, crash, node CPU/memory pressure, and OOM; contradicted by normal events, Running state, zero restarts, 7% CPU and 16% memory node usage. DNS/connectivity could not be directly tested because exec was forbidden.
dueDiligence.confidenceCalibration: 0.82: start 1.0; -0.10 because pod exec was RBAC-forbidden and direct connectivity was not verified; -0.05 because Prometheus timed out; -0.03 because NetworkPolicy enforcement by the active CNI was not directly observable. Backend, workload, event, and node evidence substantially supports the diagnosis.

contributingFactors: traffic-gen readiness probe and loop changed from successful to repeated failed health-check requests
NetworkPolicy default-network-policy selects all pods and enables ingress policy with no allowed ingress sources
web-frontend has healthy replicas, ready endpoints, and returns HTTP 200 for /healthz
Packet-level enforcement could not be directly verified because connectivity and Prometheus checks were unavailable

kaResponse.analysis: The traffic-gen replica is unavailable because its readiness probe and application loop repeatedly fail against web-frontend:8080/healthz. The namespace deny-all ingress NetworkPolicy selects all pods and is consistent with blocking the required traffic path, while the backend service and application are healthy.

rootCauseAnalysis.summary: The traffic-gen replica is unavailable because its readiness probe and application loop repeatedly fail against web-frontend:8080/healthz. The namespace deny-all ingress NetworkPolicy selects all pods and is consistent with blocking the required traffic path, while the backend service and application are healthy.
causalChain: Why? The sole Pod `traffic-gen-6fbdd9f844-c7cqm` is Running but readiness is False, and its readiness probe targets `web-frontend.demo-frontend:8080/healthz`.
Why? The traffic generator's own logs show `probe=success` initially, then repeated `probe=failure`, while the web Deployment remains 2/2 Ready with ready Service endpoints.

Why? Namespace NetworkPolicy `default-network-policy` selects every pod and enables ingress policy without any ingress allow rules, blocking ingress to selected pods; this is consistent with the probe failure.

Root cause: `demo-frontend/default-network-policy` has an ingress-isolation configuration with no allowed ingress sources, preventing the traffic-gen readiness path from succeeding. Direct packet-level confirmation was unavailable because pod exec and Prometheus access were blocked.

dueDiligence.targetAccuracy: The target is the NetworkPolicy whose ingress configuration must be changed to allow the required traffic, rather than the Deployment that only reports the symptom. A workflow can add a narrowly scoped ingress allowance.
dueDiligence.proportionality: The issue is isolated to the readiness path and has a specific policy configuration fix. The NetworkPolicy is more precise than changing replica counts, probe timing, or the healthy web Deployment. Any required ingress exception should be narrowly scoped to the relevant traffic.
dueDiligence.scopeCompleteness: Inspected the incident Deployment, owning ReplicaSet and Pod, its events/logs/current and previous-log path, downstream Service, EndpointSlice, web Deployment and two representative web Pod logs, ConfigMap, NetworkPolicy, node usage, and owner/remediation context. Prometheus was attempted but inaccessible; packet-level tests were blocked.
dueDiligence.causalCompleteness: Traced Deployment -> ReplicaSet -> Pod -> readiness probe -> downstream Service/Endpoints -> NetworkPolicy. The deepest verified configuration cause is the empty ingress allow-list in `default-network-policy`; exact CNI enforcement and packet direction could not be verified.
dueDiligence.evidenceSufficiency: Deployment, ReplicaSet, Pod, Service, EndpointSlice, downstream Deployment, ConfigMap, events, node metrics, and NetworkPolicy were inspected. Evidence supports readiness failure and healthy backend. Assumptions: the observed NetworkPolicy is enforced by the active network plugin and is the specific blocker. Pod exec was forbidden (`create pods/exec`); Prometheus discovery/series timed out; node stats-summary was forbidden (`get nodes/proxy`).
dueDiligence.regressionAwareness: No prior remediation history is available for `demo-frontend/NetworkPolicy/default-network-policy`; the target context showed no tier-1 or tier-2 remediations and no regression detected.
dueDiligence.alternativeHypotheses: Considered unhealthy web backend and missing Service endpoints; contradicted by `web-frontend` 2/2 Ready, two ready EndpointSlice entries, HTTP-200 `/healthz` ConfigMap, and clean startup logs. Considered scheduling, image pull, crash, node CPU/memory pressure, and OOM; contradicted by normal events, Running state, zero restarts, 7% CPU and 16% memory node usage. DNS/connectivity could not be directly tested because exec was forbidden.
dueDiligence.confidenceCalibration: 0.82: start 1.0; -0.10 because pod exec was RBAC-forbidden and direct connectivity was not verified; -0.05 because Prometheus timed out; -0.03 because NetworkPolicy enforcement by the active CNI was not directly observable. Backend, workload, event, and node evidence substantially supports the diagnosis.
